title: Polynomial-time payload map
statement: Let $g$ be a polynomial-time computable function from bit strings to bit strings. The function that maps a valid pair encoding of $a,b$ to the pair encoding of $a,g(b)$, and maps every string that is not a valid pair encoding to the empty string, is polynomial-time computable.
replaced: Let $g$ be a polynomial-time computable function on bit strings (computed by some finite binary Turing machine within $C(n+1)^c$ steps on inputs of length $n$, for some constants $C, c$). Then its threaded payload map, which sends a pair encoding $\langle a,b\rangle$ (every bit of $a$ doubled, then $01$, then $b$) to $\langle a, g(b)\rangle$ and every bit string that is not a pair encoding to the empty word, is also polynomial-time computable.
